rationale: The Old English suffix -ness forms abstract nouns denoting qualities or states (e.g., gōdnes 'goodness'), which aligns with the content-word sense of noun.n.01 — a word referring to a quality or thing — rather than the purely grammatical/word-class definition in noun.n.02. The gloss token 'noun' here describes the part of speech of the derived form, pointing to the concrete referential sense.
